messages:
nisha: quick question — should we prefer a redact-first model for low-volume tenant routes? thinking about CPU cost vs. legal safety.

samir: curious what you mean by redact-first here? scrub at the edge before any logging or at the proxy after routing?

nisha: scrub at the edge (api-gateway) so nothing downstream ever sees raw PII. advantage: smaller blast radius, simpler compliance story. downside: we lose ability to re-run non-destructive debug that needs raw inputs.

aj: redact-first reduces our ops exposure but it might break some existing canary debug flows. we rely on raw payloads for a small % of traces when debugging model hallucinations.

maria: can we compromise with per-tenant breakglass? default redact-first, and a short-lived breakglass token that temporarily allows pre-scrub capture?

nisha: yeah exactly — proposal: default redact-first per-route, with audit-gated breakglass that requires 2-person approval in console and writes an immutable audit event. token TTL 30m.

aj: sounds good. how do we implement pseudonymization for logs? hashing alone is reversible in some cases.

samir: use HMAC with tenant-specific key stored in KMS + per-tenant salt. HMAC(PII, tenant-key) gives stable pseudonym for a tenant but not reversible without key.

maria: tenant-key management: for hosted customers we store keys in our KMS; for private deployments they bring their own KMS/HSM. make this explicit in docs.

nisha: console UX: admin page shows a route-level toggle: "Redact-first (recommended)" with a small "breakglass" button next to it. click -> popup shows required approvers and TTL, then generates ephemeral token.

aj: please add an ops-only override for emergencies that logs who used it and emits an alert to #oncall.

nisha: yes — devops-bot will post a structured alert: `devops-bot: BREAKGLASS used by @aj on route /v2/classify tenant acme-corp ttl 30m — audit_id=abc123`.

samir: telemetry implications: redact-first reduces cardinality in our logs for sensitive fields which is good for storage/cost. BUT it also reduces signal for the dashboard heatmaps we use to detect input distribution shifts.

maria: proposal: mirror a tiny telemetry-only fingerprint: compute a 64-bit stable bucket hash of the full input (not reversible) and store that in metric pipelines (not in textual logs). use it to drive distribution charts but never make it human-readable.

aj: we need to be explicit about retention: redact logs (and pseudonyms) kept for 90 days by default, with enterprise option for longer. metrics (counts/histograms) are aggregated and retained per existing policy.

nisha: config snippet for route YAML I mocked up:
```
route: /v2/classify
redaction:
  mode: redact-first
  breakglass: true
  breakglass_ttl: 30m
  pseudonymization: hmac-kms
  hmac_key_id: projects/redwood/keys/tenant-123
```

samir: implementation note: edge should only apply structured redaction rules (email, phone, ssn) + fallback full-string HMAC. avoid naive regex-only approach.

maria: ops ask: will this increase latency at the gateway? we should benchmark. maybe run redact-first for a small canary of tenants first.

nisha: agreed. rollout plan: 1) unit tests + local bench; 2) canary on 1% low-volume tenants with console opt-in toggle; 3) monitor error rate, p95 gateway latency, and heatmap fidelity over 2 weeks; 4) expand to 25% then global.

aj: add guardrail: if gateway latency delta > 8% OR debug signal loss > 12% we rollback. metrics tracked in console rollout dashboard.

maria: tiny UI nit: show estimated cost impact in the toggle tooltip (expected storage reduction %) — helps sales/CS explain tradeoffs.

nisha: okay I'll write an RFC with the config, KMS model, breakglass flow, and rollout plan. pinging @devops-bot to create a tracking ticket. :railway_track: 

devops-bot: Created issue INF-7312: "redact-first per-route + breakglass + hmac pseudonymization" — https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-7312

samir: one more: EU customers sometimes require pseudonymization that is reversible for lawful reasons under a DPA. we should add an opt-in reversible encryption mode for enterprise only, requiring customer's KMS to hold the key.

nisha: noted. will add reversible-mode section to RFC and highlight legal approvals required.

maria: 👍 let's keep the console UX simple but surface the important guardrails.

aj: thanks — looking forward to RFC.

nisha: thanks all, I'll post draft tomorrow.
